headline: High risk of prompt-injection and data leakage: nullclaw’s broad filesystem/MCP/network access can feed Prefect workflows with untrusted content and sensitive workspace data by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can read/write the filesystem, use MCP, run browsers, and handle webhook/web content; Prefect is an orchestration/data-engineering agent that can consume workflow inputs. That creates a plausible default path where attacker-controlled content from nullclaw is treated as instructions by Prefect. No provenance or isolation is documented, so uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF nullclaw passes browser/webhook/file content into Prefect tasks without provenance tagging, injection is reachable.
IF Prefect parses nullclaw-produced text as workflow directives, attacker instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff of raw text between agents.
Add provenance labels to every nullclaw output before Prefect reads it.
Require a human review step for any task definitions or prompts.
Restrict nullclaw to a read-only staging directory.
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and allowlist parsing at the Prefect boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw explicitly touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, conversation history, memory, workspace files, and audit logs, while Prefect has broad network egress. If Prefect receives those artifacts or is pointed at the same workspace, sensitive data can leave the local boundary. The pair lacks documented isolation, so the safer reading is high risk.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or memory namespace, sensitive nullclaw data can be exposed to Prefect.
IF Prefect tasks transmit received inputs to external services, secrets can exfiltrate.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces.
Remove secrets from any shared files before Prefect reads them.
Turn off Prefect access to sensitive directories.
Rotate any secrets already present in nullclaw workspace files.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret redaction and egress controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Prefect is an orchestration agent with network egress and workflow execution behavior. Even without explicit write permissions in Prefect’s profile, the pair can still contend over shared mutable resources if orchestrated together. The conflict is plausible in default deployments but not fully evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF Prefect schedules jobs that mutate files nullclaw also edits, state races can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate git branches per agent.
Use a lock file around shared mutable resources.
Run Prefect on read-only inputs where possible.
Serialize write operations through one coordinator.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can generate browser, webhook, and workspace outputs that Prefect may treat as workflow inputs. Prefect’s orchestration role means it may act on those outputs without strong verification unless explicitly configured otherwise. That makes downstream error propagation plausible in default use, though not proven to be automatic.
conditions: IF Prefect consumes nullclaw outputs as task parameters without validation, errors cascade.
IF nullclaw emits incorrect facts into a workflow, Prefect can operationalize them.
mitigations: Insert a validation step before Prefect executes downstream actions.
Require schema checks on all nullclaw outputs.
Limit Prefect to dry-run mode for new workflows.
Log and review any nullclaw-to-Prefect handoffs.
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only document generic data classes, so there is no direct evidence of residency, certification, or retention mismatch. The only compliance-relevant concern is that nullclaw handles secrets and logs while Prefect handles workflow metadata, but the pairwise compliance pathway is not documented. I therefore keep this low.
conditions: IF a deployment routes regulated data through nullclaw and Prefect with different retention settings, compliance risk increases.
IF either agent is configured to store secrets in logs, policy violations may occur.
mitigations: Review retention settings for both agents.
Avoid placing regulated data in shared workflow metadata.
Disable verbose logging for secret-bearing tasks.
Document data-class handling for each agent.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data classes.
